name: FSUSB42MUX
title: Low-power two-port high-speed USB 2.0 (480 Mbps) switch, DPDT
summary: A bidirectional double-pole double-throw switch that routes one USB 2.0 data pair (D+, D−) to either of two source pairs, HSD1 or HSD2, chosen by SEL; OE high opens both paths. It suits high-speed (480 Mbps) and full-speed (12 Mbps) signalling, with 3.7 pF typical on capacitance, 3.9 Ω typical on resistance and 720 MHz typical bandwidth. The switch pins withstand up to 5.25 V with VCC at 0 V, and supply current stays low when the control inputs sit below VCC. It runs from 2.4 V to 4.4 V and comes in a 10-lead UQFN (UMLP) 1.4 × 1.8 mm and a 10-lead MSOP.

circuits.title: On resistance
circuits.description: A DC source VSW sets the HSDn side of a closed switch; a current source pulls ION out of Dn to ground. A voltmeter across HSDn and Dn reads VON, and RON = VON / ION. The select input sits at 0 or VCC.

parts.note: current source, current out of Dn

notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.

circuits.title: Off leakage
circuits.description: The switch is open. The HSDn side is left unconnected and an ammeter from Dn to a DC source VSW reads the leakage IDn(OFF). The select input sits at 0 or VCC. Every switch port is measured on its own.
notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.

circuits.title: AC test circuit load
circuits.description: Timing load for tON, tOFF and tPD. A DC source VSW drives HSDn; Dn carries CL and RL in parallel to ground and VOUT is read there. A pulse generator VSEL drives the control input through RS. RL, RS and CL take the values of the AC tables; CL counts the fixture and stray capacitance.
notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.
tON and tOFF are given from S or OE; SEL stands for the control input driven.

circuits.title: Break-before-make interval timing
circuits.description: Both throws are held at DC: VSW1 on one HSD input and VSW2 on the other, 0.8 V each. Dn drives CL and RL to ground and VOUT is read there. A pulse generator VSEL steps SEL through RS; tBBM is the time VOUT spends below 0.9 × VOUT during changeover.
notes: HSD1+ and HSD2+ stand for the two throws of either pole, D+ for its common pin.

circuits.title: Bandwidth
circuits.description: A network analyzer source VS with source resistance RS drives Dn through a coaxial cable; the selected HSDn returns through a second cable to the analyzer input, terminated in RT, where VOUT is read against VIN. A DC level VSEL holds the select input.
notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.
RS and RT take the values of the AC tables (RL = 50 Ω).

circuits.title: Channel off isolation
circuits.description: As the bandwidth fixture, with the channel open and Dn also terminated in RT to ground. The analyzer drives Dn through a cable and reads what reaches the open HSDn through the second cable into RT; off isolation = 20 log (VOUT / VIN).
notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.
RS and RT take the values of the AC tables (RL = 50 Ω, f = 240 MHz).

circuits.title: Non-adjacent channel-to-channel crosstalk
circuits.description: Two poles are used. The analyzer source drives the common pin of one pole (D−) through a cable, and its throw (HSD1−) is terminated in RT. The other pole's common pin (D+) is left open, and its throw (HSD1+) goes through a cable to the analyzer input across RT, where the coupled signal VOUT is read. A DC level VSEL holds the select input.
notes: The two poles stand for any pair of non-adjacent channels.
RS and RT take the values of the AC tables (RL = 50 Ω, f = 240 MHz).

circuits.title: Channel off capacitance
circuits.description: A capacitance meter on HSDn with OE high, so the switch is open, and Dn left unconnected. S is low or high.
notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.

circuits.title: Channel on capacitance
circuits.description: A capacitance meter on HSDn with OE low, so the switch is closed, and Dn left unconnected. S is low or high.
notes: HSD1+ stands for any HSDn pin and D+ for its common Dn pin.

operation.text: Each of the two poles (D+ and D−) is a two-way switch. With OE low, SEL low links D+ to HSD1+ and D− to HSD1−; SEL high links them to HSD2+ and HSD2−. With OE high, every path is open whatever SEL is. Changeover is break-before-make, with tBBM of 2.0 ns minimum. The signal path is bidirectional.

SEL and OE may be driven from a logic level below VCC with little extra supply current: ICCT is 15 µA at most with a 1.8 V control level and VCC at 4.3 V, and 10 µA at most with 2.6 V. Control lines can come straight from a baseband processor's general-purpose I/O. Thresholds are 1.3 V high and 0.5 V low for VCC from 2.4 V to 3.6 V, and 1.7 V and 0.7 V at VCC = 4.3 V. A control input must never float.
With VCC at 0 V the switch I/O pins withstand up to 5.25 V without outside parts (absolute maximum VSW, VCC = 0 V), and leak at most 2 µA from 0 V to 4.3 V (IOFF).

The 720 MHz typical bandwidth (550 MHz with 5 pF load) passes the third harmonic of a 480 Mbps signal, keeping edge and phase distortion low. On capacitance is 3.7 pF typical, intra-pair skew 20 ps typical and total jitter 200 ps typical at 480 Mbps. Off isolation is −30 dB and crosstalk between non-adjacent channels −45 dB, both at 240 MHz.

Human body model rating is 7 kV on all pins, 8 kV I/O to ground, 9 kV on D+ and D− and 16 kV from power to ground. The D+ and D− pins meet IEC 61000-4-2 system level at 15 kV air and 8 kV contact discharge. Charged device model is 2 kV.

tON and tOFF are measured from the control input (VOE or VSEL) driven from GND to VCC with 2.5 ns edges, to the output at 90% of its swing between VOL and VOH. tPD is taken between the 50% points of input and output, with a 0 V to 400 mV input and 500 ps edges. Intra-pair skew tSK(P) uses a differential ±400 mV input with 500 ps edges and compares the high-to-low and low-to-high delays of the two lines at their crossing. tBBM runs from the falling edge of the output past 0.9 × VOUT to its recovery past 0.9 × VOUT after a 2.5 ns VSEL step, with both throws held at 0.8 V.
Uses named for the part: sharing one USB connector between two sources in phones, PDAs, cameras, printers, notebooks, LCD monitors, TVs and set-top boxes.
